text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

The panel's composition is a dead end. Both you and the appointee are women, so sex cannot readily explain why she was preferred over you. Raising it would weaken your credibility on the point that actually matters.

That point is strong: on paper you appear better qualified — a master's in educational leadership versus unspecified "courses," plus five years of actual leadership experience. A panel can weigh teaching experience heavily, but it must justify doing so.

Focus on the unanswered request. In most systems an applicant is entitled to a reasoned written explanation within a set period, and two weeks of silence is itself a procedural failing. Send a written follow-up citing the relevant provision, then assess the stated reasons.
